holidays.name: International Tongue Twister Day
holidays.description: Today is for mangling your mouth on purpose. Rattle off "toy boat" five times fast, then try "red lorry, yellow lorry" and see how far you get. Give it a go and laugh at your own slip-ups.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and its origin is unclear. It has become a popular fixture on fun-holiday calendars. Teachers, speech coaches, and word nerds like it as an excuse to play with language.
holidays.funFact: "toy boat" is a sneaky tongue twister because your mouth has to switch quickly between similar sounds. The repeated rhythm makes the slip-ups more likely.

holidays.name: National Cappuccino Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates the classic Italian coffee drink: espresso, steamed milk, and a cloud of foam. Treat yourself to a cup, practice your latte-art skills, or finally learn the difference between a cappuccino and a latte.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food-and-drink observance, and its exact origin is unclear. The drink gets its name from Italy's Capuchin friars. The color of their brown robes resembles the color of the coffee.
holidays.funFact: A traditional Italian cappuccino is usually a morning drink. Many Italians avoid ordering one after a big meal, and a cappuccino after dinner can earn you some side-eye in Italy.

holidays.name: National Dunce Day
holidays.description: This is a day for celebrating the dunce cap, one of the most infamous pieces of headgear in history. It's also a nudge to be kind to your own "duh" moments. Wear a pointy hat, laugh at your goofs, and remember that everyone is a beginner at something.
holidays.origin: The day is linked to the death of the medieval scholar John Duns Scotus on November 8, 1308. His followers, the Scotists, were once admired thinkers. Later critics mocked their ideas, and the word "dunce" came to mean a slow learner.
holidays.funFact: The word "dunce" comes from the name of one of the most brilliant minds of the Middle Ages. Duns Scotus's name ended up as an insult.
